issue.title: replace tool converts literal Python newline escapes into source newlines
issue.body:
While implementing offline harness regressions, the `replace` tool reported success but converted literal backslash-n sequences in `new_string` into physical newlines inside Python string literals. The next warnings-as-errors unittest run failed with `SyntaxError: unterminated f-string literal`.

Example intended source: `self.assertIn(f"WINECAP|{attempt.name}|exit_requested|{exit_code}\n", text)`. Reading the file immediately afterward showed the string split across two source lines. The same operation split `"\n".join(...)` and a diagnostic string. Existing escaped strings outside the replacement remained unchanged.

Environment: LLxprt Code on macOS, gpt-6-astra via codex. The tool contract requires exact literal replacement. Please preserve supplied backslashes instead of interpreting source-language escape sequences.

Local evidence: stranded branch-2 `tmp/wine-setup/harness-fixes/evidence-native/verify-sqbizdgh/normal.log`; affected test source lines 376–426 immediately after the replacement.

steps: Create sample.py with exactly this one-line Python source and a final newline: value = "old". Read it with read_file.

Use the built-in replace tool to replace the complete source line with exactly the following text (backslashes are literal source characters):
value = "\n".join(["a", "b"])
Then inspect the actual file bytes.
expected: Exact replacement preserves literal source-code escape sequences after JSON decoding.
defect: replace writes physical newline/CR control characters where new_string contained literal backslash escape sequences, corrupting source code.
Root cause: The observed behavior is consistent with an additional escape-normalization step after JSON decoding, which makes literal backslash-n indistinguishable from an actual newline. The reports do not identify a confirmed implementation line; do not label an arbitrary edit helper as the root cause.
